rounds.proof_sketch: M=1024=32×32, K=4096=32×128. For loading A tile: row∈[0,1023]<1024=M always, and t*32+threadIdx.x∈[0,4095]<4096=K always. The else branch containing the mutation is never executed because both if-conditions are always satisfied.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation is on line 31 in the else branch that zeros out-of-bounds shared memory entries when loading matrix A. With M=1024 and K=4096 both being exact multiples of TILE_SIZE=32, every thread in every block is always within bounds. The row index ranges [0,1023] which is always <1024=M. The K-dimension index t*32+threadIdx.x ranges [0,4095] which is always <4096=K. Therefore, the if-condition is always true and the else branch (where threadIdx.x was mutated to threadIdx.z) is never executed, making the mutation behaviorally indistinguishable.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape contract. Would require shapes where M or K are not multiples of 32 to trigger the boundary-handling else branch.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing tiled GPU kernels, ensure test shapes include dimensions that are NOT exact multiples of the tile size to exercise boundary-handling code paths. For this kernel, testing with shapes like M=1000 or K=4000 would expose the mutated else branch.
